item.title: Flying Fijians intensify preparations ahead of Japan clash
item.description: The Fiji Water Flying Fijians are stepping up their preparations for their upcoming challenge against Japan, with the team focused on getting their plans right both on and off the field. Speaking from the Urayasu D-Rocks Training Fields, Assistant Coach Ifereimi Rawaqa says the team has completed its morning clarity session and is preparing for a big training session this afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Water Flying Fijians are stepping up their preparations for their upcoming challenge against Japan, with the team focused on getting their plans right both on and off the field.

Speaking from the Urayasu D-Rocks Training Fields, Assistant Coach Ifereimi Rawaqa says the team has completed its morning clarity session and is preparing for a big training session this afternoon.

Rawaqa says the players are sticking to their plans and making sure they look after themselves first as they continue their preparations.

The focus now is on putting in the hard work while ensuring the players are physically and mentally ready for the challenge ahead.

The Flying Fijians are continuing to build towards their match in Japan, with the coaching staff and players working together to ensure they are well prepared.

The team says the journey continues with the support of the nation.

Flying Fijians set for Japan clash at 10.05pm this Saturday.

item.title: Nadi and Nadroga set for Skipper Cup showdown
item.description: The battle of the West takes centre stage in the Skipper Cup this week, with table-toppers Nadi set to face Nadroga at King Charles Park in Nadi. The former Skipper Cup champions will be looking to hand Nadi their first defeat of the season.
item.content:encoded:
The battle of the West takes centre stage in the Skipper Cup this week, with table-toppers Nadi set to face Nadroga at King Charles Park in Nadi.

The former Skipper Cup champions will be looking to hand Nadi their first defeat of the season.

In other matches, Ba will host Naitasiri at the 4R Stadium in Ba, while Tailevu will face Lautoka at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori.

Kadavu will play Taveuni on the Garden Island at Taveuni, while Suva will face Malolo at the Suva Grammar School Ground.

Rewa will take on Navosa at the Burebasaga Grounds in Rewa.

The Under-20 fixtures will start at 1pm, with the same fixtures being played at the same grounds.

item.title: Samoa defeat Fiji Pearls 56-50 in closely fought contest
item.description: The Fiji Pearls have suffered a 56-50 defeat to Samoa this afternoon in the Netball World Cup 2027 Sydney Qualifier – Oceania in Tonga, following a closely fought contest. Fiji fought hard to mount a comeback and kept the pressure on until the final whistle, but Samoa maintained its composure to secure the six-goal victory.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Pearls have suffered a 56-50 defeat to Samoa this afternoon in the Netball World Cup 2027 Sydney Qualifier – Oceania in Tonga, following a closely fought contest.

Fiji fought hard to mount a comeback and kept the pressure on until the final whistle, but Samoa maintained its composure to secure the six-goal victory.

Both teams produced a determined performance, with Fiji unable to close the gap in the final stages of the match.

The Pearls will look to bounce back tomorrow when they face Tonga at 3pm.

They will then take on Papua New Guinea on Friday.

item.title: Tailevu and Kadavu celebrate traditional bond through ‘Na i Vakamamaca’
item.description: The traditional bond between Tailevu and Kadavu was celebrated through rugby as Tailevu supporters presented the “Na i Vakamamaca” to their Kadavu counterparts, on a day Tailevu maintained their unbeaten run in the Skipper Cup with a 30-10 victory at the Nakelo District Grounds. Fresh Choice Tailevu defeated Kadavu 30-10 at the Burebasaga grounds in Round 7 of the Skipper Cup.
item.content:encoded:
The traditional bond between Tailevu and Kadavu was celebrated through rugby as Tailevu supporters presented the “Na i Vakamamaca” to their Kadavu counterparts, on a day Tailevu maintained their unbeaten run in the Skipper Cup with a 30-10 victory at the Nakelo District Grounds.

Fresh Choice Tailevu defeated Kadavu 30-10 at the Burebasaga grounds in Round 7 of the Skipper Cup.

Tailevu Rugby says its supporters also proudly presented the “Na i Vakamamaca” to their Naita from Kadavu Rugby, reflecting the respect, unity and strong relationship between the two Timi ni Vanua Vakaturaga.

Tailevu Men’s Senior Team captain Ro Emori Imanueli Logavatu says the occasion highlights that rugby is about more than what happens on the field, as it also brings together the vanua, communities and supporters.

Meanwhile, Tailevu Team Manager Pita Naidrolevu says while they are pleased with the victory over Kadavu, the team will head back to the drawing board to work on areas that need improvement as they continue their Skipper Cup campaign.

Naidrolevu has also thanked the team’s sponsors and the Vanua for their immense support, which he says continues to drive the team forward.

Meanwhile, Tailevu is currently ranked second on the Skipper Cup standings after seven rounds of the competition while Nadi is leading with 30 points.
